candidates.label: Use strict first-vertical ceilings per invocation: 32 MiB linear memory, 4,096 table elements, one instance, 1 MiB input, 1 MiB output, 64 KiB structured logs, 10 million deterministic fuel units, 2-second wall watchdog, and one concurrent component invocation per daemon.

Use balanced first-vertical ceilings per invocation: 64 MiB linear memory, 8,192 table elements, one instance, 4 MiB input, 4 MiB output, 256 KiB structured logs, 50 million deterministic fuel units, 5-second wall watchdog, and two concurrent component invocations per daemon.

Use throughput-oriented first-vertical ceilings per invocation: 256 MiB linear memory, 32,768 table elements, one instance, 16 MiB input, 16 MiB output, 1 MiB structured logs, 250 million deterministic fuel units, 30-second wall watchdog, and four concurrent component invocations per daemon.
Allow components to allocate memory, consume CPU, emit output, log, and run concurrently without explicit ceilings or cancellation deadlines.
rejectionReasons: Unbounded guest resources contradict the selected fail-closed extension boundary and permit one component to exhaust daemon memory, CPU, output storage, or scheduling capacity.

candidates.label: Defer numeric ceilings until benchmark evidence exists; component execution and the first-vertical system binding remain blocked in the meantime.
Stop the architecture campaign while preserving the selected pure-proposal capability profile and Wasmtime host baseline.
